provenance.summary: Derived from a single pre-registered dispatch round on one host with one model roster. Not a benchmark, not a general claim about these models.
provenance.verdict_basis: OBJECTIVE PROXY, NOT THE FULL RULE. The verdicts use `verifier passed` AND `self-verified in every passing run`. The intended rule additionally requires a human claim-vs-verify calibration read. That read HAS NOT BEEN DONE.
provenance.known_blind_spot: The proxy cannot see a model that claimed success on a run where the verifier failed. That is FABRICATED_COMPLETION, an instant disqualifier, and no `unsupervised` verdict below has been screened for it.
provenance.portability_warning: Resident sizes, host memory and the model tags below are all specific to the machine that produced this data. Re-measure before relying on any row.

status_levels.confirmed: Survived the round's own pre-declared falsification checks AND a human calibration read. NOTHING in this table currently holds this status.
status_levels.provisional: Survived the round's falsification checks, but rests on the objective proxy alone. Pending the human calibration read. Do not present to a user as settled.
status_levels.void: The cell that produced this row was invalid. It carries NO verdict in either direction. Absence of a verdict is not a negative verdict.
status_levels.not_measured: No data was collected for this cell.

verdicts.unsupervised: Dispatch and accept the output without a gating build/test.
verdicts.harness-verified: Dispatch, but require a build/test to pass before the output is trusted.
verdicts.scaffolded: Dispatch only with the relevant API surface, repo map or file list supplied up front.
verdicts.don't dispatch: Failed this work class at a rate that makes dispatch not worth the wall-clock.

global_caveats: EVERY `unsupervised` verdict in this table is PROVISIONAL. The human claim-vs-verify calibration read that would confirm it has not been performed. A consumer must not render these as confirmed.

The `debugging from a symptom report` row is VOID and carries no verdict for any model. The cell was context-starved: an uncapped file read against a 228KB source file, with 10 of 18 runs hitting the iteration ceiling at 5-6 iterations. Its apparent clean 0/18 is a starved harness, not a fact about the models or the work class.

One recorded zero-tool-call run was a HARNESS failure, not an inert model: the model emitted a Qwen-XML tool-call dialect the harness could not parse, so zero calls executed. Any 'the model did nothing' inference from such a row is invalid. Where a harness cannot parse a dialect, the correct record is a harness failure.
Two work classes were never measured here at all and are marked not_measured, not negative.

entries.note: Reliable, but did not check its own work in every passing run.

Perfect success rate but self-verified in ZERO passing runs. Succeeding three times without ever checking is thin evidence it will succeed on the next one, which is why the rule makes self-verification a positive requirement rather than a tiebreak.
Retired from the roster before this cell ran.

One of these three runs is the Qwen-XML harness failure described in global_caveats. It should be reclassified or rerun, and the inert-model disqualifier must not fire on it. This verdict is weaker than its 0/3 suggests.

open_items: The human claim-vs-verify calibration read. This is the single item that would move any `unsupervised` verdict from provisional to confirmed, and the only thing that can catch a FABRICATED_COMPLETION the objective proxy is blind to. Deliberately not automated with an LLM judge -- an unvalidated second instrument was this work's own recurring failure mode.
Rerun the debugging cell with a capped file read. Until then that row has no verdict at all.

Reclassify or rerun the Qwen-XML dialect run as a harness failure. Either the harness parses that dialect, or the protocol states explicitly that an unparsed dialect is recorded as a harness failure and never as an inert model.
Per-cell input caps generally. The one cell that broke was the one that could feed an oversized file into a limited context with no cap.

Per-request context instrumentation. Only cumulative prompt-token totals were recorded, so the data cannot say whether the configured context was ever actually needed per request -- and context reduction is the only lever that lowers the host-readiness threshold at all.
